  • Immunity to one damage type, magic school, or condition
  • Weakness 10 to one damage type other than mental
  • Resistance 10 to physical damage, with an exception for either cold iron or silver
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.etMnv73EIdEZrYYu]{Frightful Presence} (aura, emotion, fear, mental) 100 feet, DC 28
  • [[/r 1d6]]{1d6} Extra Damage on Strikes, of a type one foe believes in
  • Additional Spells @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IqJ9URobmJ9L9UBG]{Shadow Blast} at 6th rank

action->Persistence of Memory.name: Persistence of Memory
action->Persistence of Memory.description: When a brainchild is destroyed, it returns if anyone still fully believes it exists, re-forming within 100 feet of any believer after [[/br 2d4 #Persistance of Memory]]{2d4 days}.

Buso Farmer.name: Buso Farmer
Buso Farmer.publicNotes:
Los Busos son una gente que vive en los árboles y que tiene un deseo ardiente de consumir la carne de los demás. Ellos complementan su alimentación con hojas y cultivos de raíces, poseen un conocimiento significativo de la agricultura, y presumen de poderes innatos sobre las plantas y su crecimiento. En cuanto a la carne, sin embargo, los busos rechazan la carne de los animales; en su lugar consumen otros humanoides. No solo les resulta repulsivo el sabor de otras criaturas, sino que sus cuerpos rechazan la carne no humanoides ya que no les proporciona ningún valor nutricional y consumirla los deja enfermos y débiles.

Las necesidades dietéticas inusuales de los busos significan que casi siempre están en desacuerdo con las culturas vecinas. Por lo general, mantienen relaciones decentes solo con los goblins, que son como un pueblo menos propenso a juzgar a otros basados en la dieta. Otras comunidades temen a los busos, con alguna justificación, aunque aparte de las incursiones ocasionales para recoger a alguien para su próxima comida, los busos tienden a mantenerse a sí mismos. En algunos lugares desesperados, las comunidades que enfrentan hambrunas u otros desastres naturales pueden incluso buscar la ayuda de los busos, ofreciendo víctimas a cambio de conocimiento o asistencia mágica que podría salvar a sus comunidades de muertes lentas y terribles por hambre.

El ojo único de un buso a veces lleva a que sean comparados con los cíclopes. Sin embargo, ambos tipos de criaturas niegan cualquier antepasado común, y aparecieron por primera vez de forma independiente en partes completamente diferentes del mundo con habilidades sustancialmente divergentes. Por su parte, los busos creen que las acciones de sus antepasados dieron lugar a sus ojos únicos. Cuando se enfrentaron a una hambruna que amenazaba su existencia, estos antepasados se cortaron uno de los ojos como ofrenda a los espíritus malignos del bosque, implorando su salvación. Los Busos dicen que estos espíritus, a quienes llaman los busaw, les dieron su conocimiento de la agricultura, el poder sobre las plantas y el ansia por carne sensible. A partir de entonces, veneraron al busaw como dioses y se llamaron a sí mismos buso: aquellos que adoran al busaw.

action->Resize Plant.name: Redimensionar la planta
action->Resize Plant.description:
Frecuencia dos veces al día.

Requisitos El buso toca una planta pequeña, mediana o grande.

Efecto La planta crece o se encoge un tamaño, permaneciendo ese tamaño por los siguientes 5 minutos. Si se usa en una criatura vegetal, este efecto tiene los efectos de @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wzctak6BxOW8xvFV]{Agrandar} o @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.PjhUmyKnq6K5uDby]{Encoger} (elección de buso). Las criaturas vegetales reacias pueden intentar un lanzamiento salvador @Check[fortitude|dc:18] para resistir este efecto.

Cactus Leshy.name: Leshy de los cactus
Cactus Leshy.publicNotes:
Estas pequeñas plantas son conocidas por su actitud urticante. Sus personalidades reflejan las espinas que brotan de todo su cuerpo, haciéndolos contenciosos y ligeramente espinosos, aunque son inquebrantablemente leales a aquellos que ganan su confianza. Habitando en paisajes secos y áridos, los cactus leshy almacenan agua dentro de sus cuerpos para sobrevivir a estas duras condiciones.

Los cactus leshys vienen en todas las formas y colores diferentes: altos y delgados, con hermosas flores de colores vibrantes en sus cabezas; en cuclillas y redondos, con filas y filas de espinas ordenadas; o aparentemente al azar, con segmentos planos apilados de extremo a extremo como si estuvieran balanceándose uno sobre el otro.

A menudo se encuentran ayudando a los practicantes de la magia de la naturaleza, los leshys son flora sensible que protegen el mundo natural y los espacios sagrados dentro de los bosques, campos y otros ambientes. Los Leshys son espíritus de la naturaleza que habitan cuerpos construidos de materia vegetal fusionada por un ritual primordial.

action->Little Oasis.name: El pequeño oasis
action->Little Oasis.description: If a cactus leshy is willing, a creature can harvest enough water from the leshy's inner cavity to fill a single waterskin without harming them. Doing so again before the leshy can replenish the water causes the leshy to immediately suffer from dehydration.

action->Spiny Body.name: Cuerpo espinoso
action->Spiny Body.description: A cactus leshy is covered in spines. A creature that @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabs} the cactus leshy takes @Damage[(1d8+3)[piercing]] damage.

action->Verdant Burst.name: Explosión verde
action->Verdant Burst.description: When a cactus leshy dies, a burst of primal energy explodes from its body, restoring @Damage[2d8[healing]] Hit Points to each plant creature in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This area sprouts cacti, becoming difficult terrain. If the terrain is not a viable environment for the cacti, they wither after 24 hours.

action->Change Shape.description:

The cactus leshy transforms into a Small cactus. This ability otherwise uses the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dileJ0Yxqg76LMvu]{One with Plants}.

action->Prickly Burst.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The cactus leshy shoots their spines in every direction. All creatures in a @Template[emanation|distance:10] take @Damage[3d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:18|basic|options:area-effect] save).

Caligni Caller.name: Caligni Caller
Caligni Caller.publicNotes:
Although the mysterious demigods known as the Forsaken disappeared eons ago, many calignis continue to follow their ancient traditions of worship.

Owbs, once the Forsaken's servants, still respond to caligni prayers. Caligni callers serve as the priests of their communities, calling upon these shadowy owb patrons for guidance, favors, and power. Their most important ceremony, the blanching, determines the potential of most newborn calignis and shapes their eventual forms.

Due to their close ties to the malevolent owbs, most callers exhibit cruel and inscrutable natures. They often lead caligni enclaves alongside caligni stalkers as spiritual advisors. Callers tend to be highly superstitious, seeing omens everywhere, and they avoid revealing details of their rituals even to other calignis.

Each individual in caligni society serves a specific role. At times, certain roles so rarely find suitable candidates that a community might only see a few individuals fill them in an entire generation.

Caligni Vanguard.name: Caligni Vanguard
Caligni Vanguard.publicNotes:
Caligni children born without eyes-an extremely rare occurrence-are considered sacred to their communities. From a young age, they're set aside and groomed to become caligni vanguards, dedicated to rigorous martial training and mental strictures. Other calignis revere vanguards' discipline and combat skill, but wary caution always tinges such respect, as they often have inscrutable motives. Vanguards almost never rebel against their duties or their established role in the community; some claim that those who do are taken by the owbs.

A vanguard's armor is fused to their body in pieces, and they rarely remove those elements that aren't. This armor plating and vanguards' keen sense of hearing render them particularly sensitive to sonic vibrations, which serves as both an asset and a vulnerability.

Each individual in caligni society serves a specific role. At times, certain roles so rarely find suitable candidates that a community might only see a few individuals fill them in an entire generation.

It is costly and heavy, and the wearer often requires help to don it correctly, but it provides some of the best defense armor can supply. A suit of this armor comes with an undercoat of padded armor and a pair of gauntlets.

action->Echolocation 60 feet.name: Echolocation 60 feet

The vanguard's armor is destroyed in the blaze, but their other gear is unaffected and left in a pile where they died.

action->Call to Arms.name: Call to Arms
action->Call to Arms.description: Each caligni within @Template[emanation|distance:30]{30 feet} of the vanguard gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.hFtNbo1LKYCoDy2O]{Attack of Opportunity} reaction until the end of the vanguard's next turn. Once a caligni has used this Attack of Opportunity, that caligni is temporarily immune to the same vanguard's Call to Arms for 10 minutes.

action->Shadowed Blade.name: Shadowed Blade
action->Shadowed Blade.description: The vanguard makes a melee Strike, channeling shadowy essence into their weapon or unarmed attack to envelop the target. If the Strike hits, the target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:19] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} until the end of its next turn.

Calikang.name: Calikang
Calikang.publicNotes:
Calikangs are giant, blue-skinned, six-armed guardians of ancient tombs and treasuries. They each feel a deep, inherent drive to protect and guard, making them highly sought after as wardens and bodyguards. Because most serve as solitary guardians, few calikang societies exist.

Calikangs' unique physiologies enable them to absorb and manipulate electrical magic as well as other energies. They can live for 200 years-though they can further extend their lives via suspended animation. For this reason, many are chosen to guard tombs or other sealed sites where living guardians would perish and constructs would deteriorate.
Calikang.saveDetails: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

action->Suspended Animation.name: Suspended Animation
action->Suspended Animation.description:
By concentrating for 5 minutes, the calikang can enter a state of suspended animation, freezing in place and becoming motionless but remaining aware of their surroundings.

While in this state, the calikang gains a +4 status bonus to Fortitude saves; doesn't age; and is immune to disease, inhaled toxins, poison, starvation, and thirst.

The calikang can exit suspended animation as a free action. If they exit this state to attack, the calikang gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative roll.

action->Energy Conversion.description:
Whenever the calikang is hit by an electricity spell's attack roll or rolls a successful save against a spell that deals electricity damage, they absorb the energy.

This heals the calikang for an amount of HP equal to quadruple the spell's rank and recharges their Breath Weapon. A calikang can't absorb their own spells this way.

These attacks count toward the calikang's multiple attack penalty, which doesn't increase until after all the attacks are complete.

For 1 round, the calikang gains a circumstance bonus to their AC equal to the number of Strikes they choose not to take, to a maximum of +4 for taking only two Strikes.

Camel.name: Camel
Camel.publicNotes:
For generations untold, nomads and traders have relied on sure-footed camels to cross the harsh deserts and trackless wastes around the world. Thriving where other animals wither and perish, camels are well-adapted to their homes with tough skin and the ability to store nutrients within their bodies. Properly cared for, these "ships of the desert" can trek for weeks between oases without trouble.

Camels have three eyelids to protect them from desert sands and other blowing debris. One lid is completely clear, which allows them to see and travel during high winds. When sandstorms strike, camels completely close their nostrils to protect their lungs. Their underbellies also sport a thick, specialized skin, allowing them to lay down safely on burning hot sands.

Contrary to popular belief, fatty tissue comprises a camel's humps rather than water. This stored energy allows the animals to survive long distances between feedings. These herbivores can also readily digest hardy scrub brush inedible to other species, making them one of the hardiest desert survivors. Strong as a warhorse, camels can run fast and even sprint for short periods of time when they feel threatened, though they prefer a slow, plodding pace to conserve energy.

One-humped camels, also called dromedaries, are more common in the deserts of northern Garund, while the two-humped variety are native to the dry steppes of Casmaron. Both species have tall and lanky builds, standing about 6 feet at the shoulder and weighing around 2,000 pounds. They can be ornery when mishandled, and they don't hesitate to bite, kick, or even spit a noxious substance on riders who don't treat them well.

In addition to transporting people and goods, camels are a key source of fiber for clothing and tents as well as milk. Their meat is highly nutritious and surprisingly tasty, but given the creatures' utility, this use is reserved for special occasions or truly dire situations.

action->Desert-Adapted.name: Desert-Adapted
action->Desert-Adapted.description: A camel is well-adapted to heat and deserts. If allowed to drink and eat its fill, (roughly 40 gallons), it can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.49y9Ec4bDii8pcD3]{Subsist} for 2 weeks without needing to attempt Survival checks, and it treats environmental heat as if it was one step less severe.

action->Camel Spit.name: Camel Spit
action->Camel Spit.description:
To drive away enemies, the camel spits the partially digested contents of its stomach at a creature within 10 feet.

On a hit, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round and must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:17] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

The camel can't use its camel spit Strike again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Camel Spit]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Sand Stride.name: Sand Stride
action->Sand Stride.description: The camel Strides twice. It has a +5-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed during these Strides, ignoring difficult terrain caused by rubble, sand, and uneven ground made of earth and stone.

Caulborn.name: Caulborn
Caulborn.publicNotes:
Profetas telepáticos e historiadores, los caulborn se reúnen en pequeñas cábalas para protección y camaradería, usando su poder cerebral colectivo para desentrañar enigmas cósmicos. Una vez que han agotado los secretos de un área, se van, buscando nuevos hogares escondidos dentro de las ciudades, secuestrando dentro de cuevas, o acechando en rincones olvidados de los planos. Desde el momento en que un ioton absorbe pensamientos especialmente profundos y comienza a tomar la forma permanente de un joven caulborn, el genio y la dureza de estos ennosites crecen con cada nuevo descubrimiento. Absorber dicha información desestabiliza su forma corporal, como cuando los libros se apilan demasiado alto, por lo que el exceso de conocimiento se filtra del cuerpo de un caulborn, causando un drenaje cerebral literal que los caulborn encuentran increíblemente molesto. Para evitar esta ocurrencia, los caulborn deben alimentarse de la energía psíquica de otros para mantenerse, lo cual es generalmente un proceso inofensivo. Especialmente hambriento caulborn incluso secuestra a la presa.

A pesar de su necesidad de alimentarse, los caulborn rara vez se preocupan por interactuar con otras criaturas, especialmente seres que podrían reaccionar a su aparición con miedo u hostilidad. Ocasionalmente hacen excepciones para los académicos o viajeros con historias, sin embargo, intercambiando su propia tradición por secretos externos.

El Plano Astral es un nexo planar, que conecta los planos de la Esfera Interior con los de la Esfera Exterior, un reino de sustancia plateada intemporal cargada con esencia mental extraída de todo el Gran Más Allá. La mayoría de las criaturas en el Plano Astral son visitantes-depredadores que buscan cazar del Río de Almas, psicopompas que protegen contra tales incursiones, y eones que monitorean el flujo de quintaesencia cruda a través de la Antípoda. Sin embargo, este plano ha engendrado criaturas nativas de sus corrientes y remolinos extraños, la más importante de las cuales es la familia de criaturas engendradas por el pensamiento conocidas como ennosites.

La forma de un ennosite físicamente encarna su pensamiento y propósito. Como algunos ideales y metas son compartidos, también lo son ciertas formas.

Cave Giant.name: Cave Giant
Cave Giant.publicNotes:
Cave giants are the vicious loners of the giant world. Even their closest ancestral kin, the rampaging hill giants, mostly find cave giants too brutal and antisocial to form alliances with. For their part, cave giants-garbed in stinking hides festooned with the rotting skulls of their victims-seem ambivalent about their foul reputation. They are more interested in hunting and killing their next meal than forming alliances.

For all their disregard of others' opinions, cave giants are cautious when it comes to defending territory. Cave giant traps are simple yet effective, such as rounded boulders that can be pushed down steep tunnels, camouflaged pits filled with sharpened stakes, and even compromised stalactites that can suddenly fall on unsuspecting intruders.

In coastal towns and hillside villages with caves a common feature of the landscape, cave giants star as common villains in local tall tales. Many youngsters and aspiring heroes dare one another to venture into remote grottoes or abandoned mine shafts in the hopes of discovering a cave giant, and all too often their searches prove successful. Grieving villagers pay skilled adventures handsomely to locate the whereabouts of their missing kin. The bounty for such hunts might be as much as an entire village harvest's worth of gold, particularly if a local cave giant has been a frequent enough menace or the missing villager is particularly beloved.

Many kinds of giants lurk in the inhospitable corners of the world, making their homes in unlikely locales ranging from fetid sinkholes and ruined battlefields to mass graveyards and barren badlands.

weapon->Greataxe.description:
tag will get replaced with text from compendium entry @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.8COlYvHe6hKCXY8x]

action->Smear.name: Smear
action->Smear.description:
Requirements The cave giant is within reach of a creature that is adjacent to a wall or other solid vertical surface

Effect The cave giant snags the creature and smashes it against the wall. The giant attempts an @Check[athletics|defense:reflex] check against the target's Reflex DC. On a success, the cave giant @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.Tkd8sH4pwFIPzqTr]{Grabs} the creature and smears it along the nearby wall, dealing @Damage[(2d8+8)[bludgeoning]] damage. On a critical success, the damage is doubled.

Cecaelia Trapper.name: Cecaelia Trapper
Cecaelia Trapper.publicNotes:
Las Cecaelias se parecen a los humanos con tentáculos de pulpo en lugar de patas. Estos cazadores oceánicos son criaturas ágiles e inteligentes, pero orgullosas. Su curiosidad a menudo los pone en contacto con extraños, donde un mal giro de frase o un insulto no intencionado puede rápidamente encender su legendario temperamento.

Las Cecaelias viven vidas nómadas, cazando y recogiendo basura a lo largo de las costas para obtener alimentos y baratijas comercializables. Participan en el comercio frecuente con las comunidades terrestres, ofreciendo cualquier cosa desde mariscos hasta tesoros recuperados de barcos hundidos a cambio de bienes que no están fácilmente disponibles bajo el agua. Algunos se dedican a la piratería o se contratan como mercenarios, pero su carácter peleador los lleva a volver a tomar su propio camino antes de que pase mucho tiempo. Las únicas comunidades no cecaelia que mantienen relaciones duraderas con las cecaelia son las de los notablemente relajados locathahs, que coexisten con las cecaelia en la ciudad de Xidao.

Las Cecaelias viven en aguas cálidas a lo largo de arrecifes oceánicos verdes o costas, a menudo cerca de asentamientos humanoides. Capaz de adaptarse rápidamente en unas pocas generaciones, las cecaelias adoptan las características físicas de sus vecinos humanoides más cercanos, que los sabios comparan con el camuflaje natural de un pulpo.

equipment->Net.description:
tag will get replaced with text from compendium entry @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.T8EopYZLT137CsdW]

You can use a net either on its own or attached to a rope. When attached to a rope, you can use the net to Grapple a Medium or smaller creature up to 10 feet away (instead of only adjacent creatures). You can continue to Grapple to keep your hold on the target so long as the target remains within 10 feet and you continue to hold the net. The grabbed creature gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Escape unless you are adjacent to them, and it can attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:16|traits:action:force-open] check to Force Open the net entirely. Once the target is no longer grabbed, the net is unwieldy until refolded as a Concentrate action that requires two hands; if used without being refolded, Grapple checks made with the net take a -2 penalty.

When the net is unattached, you can attempt a ranged attack roll against a Medium or smaller creature within 20 feet. On a hit, the target is off-guard and takes a -10- foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it Escapes, and on a critical hit, it's also immobilized until it Escapes. The Escape DC is 16 ([[/act escape dc=16]]). A creature adjacent to the target can Interact to remove the net.

Las criaturas dentro de la nube son @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{No detectado} criaturas que usan la vista u olfato, y no pueden ver u oler mientras están dentro de la nube. Chouchin-Obake.name: Chouchin-Obake
Chouchin-Obake.publicNotes:
Un chouchin-obake toma la forma de una linterna de papel con una hendidura horizontal cerca de la parte inferior de la que sobresale una larga lengua. Tras una inspección más cercana, dos ojos aparecen sobre la boca dividida. Los Chouchin-obake son anómalos en que no despiertan de la misma manera que otros tsukumogami. Las linternas de papel son casi imposibles de mantener durante el tiempo suficiente para generar tsukumogami. En cambio, un chouchin-obake es un tipo de kami de fuego que toma la forma de la llama de una linterna y habita una linterna de papel cuando se manifiestan.

Los Tsukumogami son objetos inteligentes y móviles formados por la unión entre un objeto de 100 años de edad y un kami. Los Tsukumogami van desde inofensivos a maliciosos, cada personalidad individual es el resultado de cómo se trató al objeto antes de su despertar. Los objetos bien cuidados tienden a dar a luz a tsukumogamis útiles y amigables, mientras que los objetos maltratados o abandonados se convierten en seres malévolos y violentos. La mayoría de los tsukumogamis son, por naturaleza, traviesos, y a menudo no quieren nada más que ocupar la atención de las criaturas vivas.

El tsukumogami se puede encontrar comúnmente en áreas con una fuerte creencia cultural en el valor de cuidar los objetos, lo que ayuda a los artículos a sobrevivir el tiempo suficiente para convertirse en tsukumogami. Las ciudades y pueblos con grandes poblaciones de tsukumogami se refieren a "ciudades sin sueño" debido a las celebraciones nocturnas de tsukumogami, que pueden llegar a ser tan ruidosas que impiden que los residentes vivos duerman pacíficamente.

action->Lifewick Candle.name: Vela de Lifewick
action->Lifewick Candle.description:
15 pies. Una llama azul fantasmal dentro del chouchin-obake se alimenta de la fuerza vital de los vivos para sostenerse a sí mismos.

Al comienzo del turno de chouchin-obake, cada criatura en el aura recibe @Damage[2d6[void]] puntos de daño ( @Check[fortitude|dc:26|basic] salvación). El chouchin-obake recupera una cantidad de Puntos de Golpe igual a la cantidad de daño recibido por la criatura que recibió más daño.

Chyzaedu.name: Chyzaedu
Chyzaedu.publicNotes: El mundo de Chyzaedus fue consumido hace milenios por el Dominio de los Negros a través de la manipulación de un agujero negro. En lugar de aceptar la destrucción o luchar, los chyzaedus unieron fuerzas con sus destructores, viendo en ellos un propósito mayor que la mera dominación mundial. Hoy en día, los chyzaedus sirven en un papel similar al de un sacerdocio para el Dominio y tienen un siniestro interés en llevar sus creencias a nuevos mundos, enseñando a los habitantes ignorantes la gloria de la destrucción entrópica pura. Al igual que los agujeros negros que veneran, los chyzaedus poseen un hambre eterna por el sustento y el conocimiento por igual - nunca pueden ser saciados por ninguno de los dos, sin embargo, nunca morirán de hambre mientras haya mortales cuya energía pueden alimentarse.

action->Alien Vestment.name: Vestimenta de Alien
action->Alien Vestment.description:
El chyzaedu lleva una extraña capa extraterrestre de moco violeta brillante que se desliza y se arrastra sobre su carne, pero es duro como el hierro al tacto.

Si un chyzaedu recibe daño de golpe de un golpe crítico, su vestidura alienígena se rompe, lo que reduce su CA a 27 y hace que pierda su resistencia al daño mental y físico; puede hacer crecer una nueva vestidura alienígena concentrándose durante 1 hour.

action->Ecstatic Hunger.name: El hambre extática
action->Ecstatic Hunger.description:
30 feet. A chyzaedu gains sustenance by feeding upon the metabolisms of organic victims. A living creature that ends its turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:27] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.

Success The creature suffers a painful hunger pang, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round.

Failure If possible, the creature spends its first 2 actions on its next turn eating or drinking (or spending actions to procure food or drink from its possessions or the surroundings, if necessary). The creature won't consume anything dangerous, but will eat things it normally has no appetite for.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature will eat or drink dangerous consumables, such as poison or rotten food, if other food or drink are not immediately available. The creature must spend its first 2 actions each round consuming for as long as it remains in the chyzaedu's aura plus 1 minute thereafter, but the creature can attempt a new saving throw at the end of its turn each round to end the effect early.

Note: A DC was not provided for this ability by Paizo. The DC present here is a moderate DC for the creature level according to the Gamemastery Guide creature building Tables.

Clacking Sea Skull Swarm.name: Enjambre de calaveras de mar clacando
Clacking Sea Skull Swarm.publicNotes:
Rodeando en las olas de la muerte blanqueada, enjambres de cráneos se levantan de los restos de docenas de humanoides decapitados. El horrible crujido de los ataques de las calaveras distrae a sus presas incluso mientras intentan huir aterrorizadas.

Un enjambre de cráneos está compuesto por masas reanimadas de cráneos y mandíbulas, formando una avalancha aterradora de furia de muertos vivientes. La mayoría de los enjambres de cráneos no tienen mente, aunque algunos conservan un vestigio de ingenio, conciencia e incluso talentos mágicos de la vida, culminando en una mente de enjambre altamente inteligente.

Clockwork Dragon.name: Clockwork Dragon
Clockwork Dragon.publicNotes:
Clockwork dragons are a marvel of clockwork design. These powerful masterpieces have the ability to fly, making them versatile and dangerous killers. A clockwork dragon's winding mechanism is more efficient than those of other clockworks, allowing it to partially reuse energy generated by flapping its wings. Creating a clockwork dragon requires not only an advanced understanding of clockwork design, but also a greater cache of rare resources, as its body requires solid reinforcement. As a result, most clockwork dragons have adamantine fortification. Creating a clockwork dragon without adamantine is entirely possible, though such dragons are typically smaller and more fragile.

Intricate, complex machines, clockworks are built with care by highly skilled engineers. Though their creation involves some amount of magic, they're primarily mechanical, packed with precision-tuned gears and springs working in concert.

The sturdy mainspring within a clockwork must be wound to provide the energy needed to power the device. Some larger clockworks contain a series of springs for different limbs that each need to be wound. A clockwork's crafter creates a unique metal key while building the clockwork; winding the clockwork usually involves inserting the key into the machine's back and turning clockwise. Larger clockworks require greater strength to turn the key, and typically have larger keys to allow for more torque-some even accommodating a team of winders rather than an individual. Programming a clockwork requires both the key and the knowledge to set the program correctly, information usually reserved for the clockwork's creator or owner.

action->Wind-Up.name: Wind-Up
action->Wind-Up.description:
1 week, [[/act disable-device dc=35]]{DC 35 Thievery}, standby

For a clockwork to act, it must be wound with a unique key by another creature. This takes 1 minute. Once wound, it remains operational for the listed amount of time, usually 24 hours, after which time it becomes unaware of its surroundings and can't act until it's wound again. Some clockworks' abilities require them to spend some of their remaining operational time. They can't spend more than they have and shut down immediately once they have 0 time remaining. If it's unclear when a clockwork was last wound, most clockwork keepers wind all their clockworks at a set time, typically 8 a.m.

A clockwork that lists standby in its wind-up entry can enter standby mode as a 3-action activity. Its operational time doesn't decrease in standby, but it can sense its surroundings (with a -2 penalty to Perception). It can't act, with one exception: when it perceives a creature, it can exit standby as a reaction (rolling initiative if appropriate).

A creature can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.cYdz2grcOcRt4jk6]{Disable a Device} to wind a clockwork down (with a DC listed in the wind-up entry). For each success, the clockwork loses 1 hour of operational time. This can be done even if the clockwork is in standby mode.

action->Self-Destruct.name: Self-Destruct
action->Self-Destruct.description:
A clockwork dragon must use this reaction unless specifically programmed otherwise by its creator.

Trigger The clockwork dragon is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Effect The dragon screeches to a stop and emits a steady, loud ticking sound. At the beginning of what would have been its next turn, the dragon explodes, dealing @Damage[12d10[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[emanation|distance:40] (@Check[reflex|dc:37|basic|options:area-effect] save).

An adjacent creature can cancel the self-destruct sequence by succeeding at a @Check[thievery|dc:37|traits:action:disable-a-device] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.cYdz2grcOcRt4jk6]{Disable a Device}.

action->Breath Weapon.name: Breath Weapon
action->Breath Weapon.description:
The clockwork dragon breathes a spray of flaming oil that deals @Damage[16d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[cone|distance:40] (@Check[reflex|dc:37|basic|options:area-effect] save).

Creatures that fail their saves are covered in burning oil and take @Damage[2d6[persistent,fire]].

The clockwork dragon can't use Breath Weapon again for 2 rounds.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Draconic Frenzy
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: The clockwork dragon makes two claw Strikes and one wing Strike in any order.

action->Spearing Tail.name: Spearing Tail
action->Spearing Tail.description:
The clockwork dragon attacks with the sharp point of its tail.

It makes a tail Strike against each creature in a @Template[line|distance:20], rolling the attack roll once and applying the result to each target. Any creature hit takes @Damage[4d6[bleed]] (@Damage[(2*4d6)[bleed]] on a critical hit). This counts as two attacks for the dragon's multiple attack penalty.

Their spindly bodies and delicate components make them unsuitable for combat; in fact, most builders construct clockwork spies with a self-destruct mechanism to ensure the spies' meddling can't be traced back to them.

action->Record Audio.name: Record Audio
action->Record Audio.description:
The clockwork spy records all sounds within @Template[emanation|distance:25]{25 feet} onto a small gemstone worth 1 gp embedded in its body. The clockwork spy can record up to 1 hour of sound on a single gemstone. Once it begins recording, it can't cease recording early, nor can it record onto a gemstone that already contains a recording.

Some clockwork spies contain multiple gemstones to allow for a series of recordings. Since clockwork spies are not intelligent, they must be given simple commands regarding when to start recording sounds. A clockwork spy can differentiate between different kinds of creatures but not between specific individuals.

The spy can start or stop playback of recorded sound by spending a single action. Removing a gemstone from or installing a gemstone into a clockwork spy requires a successful [[/act disable-device dc=14]]{DC 14 Thievery} check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.cYdz2grcOcRt4jk6]{Disable a Device}; on a failure, the gemstone is undamaged, but any recorded sounds are erased and the gemstone still can't be used to make another recording.

Common Eurypterid.publicNotes:
El más pequeño de los euriptéridos gigantes puede crecer hasta el tamaño de un perro grande. Estos eurypterids son un alimento básico para las personas que viven en los pantanos, que añaden la carne a los guisos fuertemente especiados, pero de lo contrario se consideran plagas peligrosas.

Depredadores temibles y plagas duraderas, los eurypterids son artrópodos de carapaces duros a veces llamados escorpiones marinos. Aunque son criaturas acuáticas, tienen sistemas respiratorios robustos que les permiten sobrevivir indefinidamente en tierra. Todos los euriptéridos poseen garras, así como aguijones que pueden inyectar veneno.

Consonite Choir.name: Coro de Consonite
Consonite Choir.publicNotes:
Inundaciones de hojas cristalinas llamadas coros de consonita surgen a través de las cavernas y túneles del Plano de la Tierra. Aunque sus resonantes campanadas pueden ser una de las músicas más bellas de los planos, aquellos que se intrometen en su territorio se enfrentan a una pared de sonido que sacude los huesos y una lluvia de cristales afilados como cuchillas.

Las cuchillas se forman naturalmente, solo uno de los muchos maravillosos tipos de cristal en el Plano de la Tierra. Las estalactitas consonitas de bordes afilados zumban y suenan junto con el movimiento de molienda del avión. A medida que grandes colecciones de estos cristales comienzan a comunicarse entre sí a través de su canción compartida, despiertan en una especie de colectivo musical.

Eventualmente, las canciones de los coros consonantes se vuelven lo suficientemente fuertes y complejas como para sacudir a estas colonias de sus amarres de piedra y liberarlas para explorar el Plano de la Tierra. Los coros consoníticos prefieren permanecer cerca de sus lugares de cría, pero pueden ser obligados a actuar en las casas de shaitans ricos o servir a otras criaturas poderosas de la tierra. Dejan voluntariamente la comodidad de sus hogares para cazar a los odiados xorns, que disfrutan del sabor de sus inmóviles hermanos consonitas.

Los coros consonantes que abandonan el Plano de la Tierra, ya sea a través de portales naturales o respondiendo a las llamadas de poderosos rituales, a menudo encuentran los espacios abiertos de otros planos más a su gusto. Disfrutan de la sensación de vientos fuertes que se mueven a través de sus campanas y buscan incansablemente a socios de actuación expertos. Destinos más crueles atrapan a otros coros, seres más poderosos podrían vincularlos místicamente al servicio o intimidarlos para convertirlos en trofeos vivientes.

Con el paso de los años, las cuchillas de cristal individuales de un coro se astillan y se rompen naturalmente. En sus cavernas nativas, los coros consonantes pueden encontrar fácilmente nuevos miembros. Atrapados en otro lugar, deben depender de otros para obtener hojas de repuesto o eventualmente caer en torpor.

Coral Capuchin.name: Coral Capuchin
Coral Capuchin.publicNotes:
A coral capuchin resembles a hairless pink monkey with large eyes and batlike wings. Something of a tropical nuisance, these amphibious creatures follow trade ships, hoping to filch small valuables they can take home or perhaps find a sailor they can befriend to secure a regular supply of food.

Coral capuchins live in tropical climates, and while they can breathe water or air with equal ease, their membranous skin means they rely heavily on having a nearby source of water. Fresh- and saltwater serve equally well for this purpose, though the creatures generally congregate near oceans and seas for other reasons. Jungles, islands, and warm coastlines are their most common nesting sites, though they usually hide their nests high in trees or in other locations out of easy reach of predators, scavengers, or anything that might steal the trinkets they've collected.

These little flyers are insatiably curious, and they love to follow humanoids around. Capuchins largely agree that humanoids have the best food and trinkets. Smarter than animals and capable of rudimentary speech, the creatures can be quite useful with the right training, learning how seek out sunken treasures or hunt down rats and other pests on a ship. Some spellcasters residing along tropical coastlines have taken coral capuchins as familiars, though many claim the critters as far more trouble than any benefits they provide are worth. A capuchin familiar might pilfer spellcasting components, gemstones, vials, crafting materials, and other trinkets from their master, though a clever magic user will intersperse more appealing (and less valuable) baubles to draw their familiar's attention away from actually important items.

Capuchin clans live together under a single matriarch, a slightly larger female who can be identified by her unusually prismatic skin and colorful eyes. These females refuse to be tamed or kept as pets and violently resist all forms of capture. The most powerful among them even possess divine powers which they call upon to protect their homes and kin. In return, the remainder of the clan fights fiercely to protect their matriarch, defending her (and her trinkets) from threats far larger than themselves.

action->Moisture Dependency.name: Moisture Dependency
action->Moisture Dependency.description: A coral capuchin must stay in or near water, or else it begins drying out. It can remain away from water for only 12 hours before its membranous skin starts to turn brittle and flake, taking @Damage[1d6[untyped]] damage per hour until it is doused in water.

action->Capuchin's Curse.name: Capuchin's Curse
action->Capuchin's Curse.description:
If a capuchin damages a creature with its jaws Strike, the creature gains both a blessing and a curse that last for [[/gmr 1d6 #Duration Capuchin's Curse]]{1d6 hours}.

While the blessing doubles the amount of time that the affected creature can hold its breath, the curse imposes a quickened version of the capuchin's moisture dependency, taking @Damage[1d6[untyped]] damage every 10 minutes they go without water.

A cursed creature can fully immerse itself in water as a 3-action activity to attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:17] save, ending both the blessing and the curse on a success.

Corrupted Relic.name: Reliquia corrupta
Corrupted Relic.publicNotes:
Las criaturas que una vez tuvieron objetos particulares queridos pueden estar ligados a ellos después de la muerte, sus almas habitan el objeto desde el interior. Estos podrían ser los fieles que persiguen los símbolos de su fe, los guerreros que se aferran a sus viejas armas, o los codiciosos que habitan su preciosa riqueza. Los cuerpos físicos de estos espíritus se han degradado desde hace mucho tiempo, pero mantienen sus corruptas reliquias prístinas. Los espíritus se manifiestan sobre los desprevenidos o curiosos, decididos a destruir a cualquiera que se atreviera a mostrar interés en su única y preciosa posesión.

Aunque son raros, hay varios tipos de reliquias corruptas. El espíritu encadenado puede manifestarse de diferentes maneras, desde animar un arma antigua hasta poseer a cualquiera que se ponga el objeto. Destruir la reliquia a menudo termina siendo la forma más simple y directa de desterrar el propio espectáculo. Destruir o disipar el espíritu sin destruir la reliquia, sin embargo, a veces puede dejar un tesoro inestimable.

El amuleto que se muestra aquí tiene los aspectos de aire y muerte. Sus dones menores, chispa mortal y mirada mortal, potencian algunas de las habilidades del espíritu. Alguien que reclama la reliquia podría ganar diferentes dones de esos aspectos.

equipment->Amulet.name: Amuleto
equipment->Amulet.description: Relics are a special type of magic item that can grow in power as their wielders unlock additional abilities. The full rules for relics and their aspects begin on page 94 of the Gamemastery Guide.

action->Amulet Relic.name: Reliquia de Amuleto
action->Amulet Relic.description:
La reliquia corrupta es un amuleto maldecido para contener un espíritu malévolo. Las estadísticas en este bloque de estadísticas son para el espíritu cuando está manifestado (ver Manifesto). El amuleto no puede tomar ninguna acción excepto Manifestación Súbita y Manifiesto. Mientras el espíritu se manifieste, el amuleto es inmune a conjuros y habilidades mágicas y usa los salvamentos que se enumeran aquí.

Independientemente de si el espíritu se manifiesta, el amuleto puede ser atacado por golpes (CA 21, Dureza 5, UR 10 ). No es incorpóreo. Si el amuleto se rompe, el espíritu está encerrado y no puede manifestarse, y si el amuleto se destruye, también lo hace el espíritu. Destruir el espíritu libera al amuleto de su maldición.

El espíritu permanece en su estado manifestado hasta que ya no percibe a ninguna criatura viviente dentro del alcance de su sentido de la vida.

Crossroads Guardian.name: Guardián de la Encrucijada
Crossroads Guardian.publicNotes:
Cuando un pueblo es amenazado por una horda de bandidos pero no hay nadie para ayudar, cuando la reliquia divina de un monasterio debe ser protegida pero el último monje está en su lecho de muerte, cuando el mundo puede ser salvado solo a través del uso de un artefacto que nadie recuerda, la naturaleza responde creando un guardián de la encrucijada, una entidad natural de magia primitiva. Cada guardián de encrucijada existe para satisfacer una necesidad particular, generalmente una búsqueda que debe llevarse a cabo, individuos indefensos que deben ser salvados de daño, o un objeto o lugar que debe ser protegido. Aunque a menudo aparecen en cruces reales, un guardián de cruces puede materializarse en cualquier lugar donde haya una comunidad, desde una metrópolis gigante hasta un pueblo de lagarto en un pantano remoto.

Algunos guardianes de cruces son seres marciales, por ejemplo, los que defienden una fuente mística contra todos los intrusos, pero la mayoría son ayudantes y asistentes, guiando a los héroes a través del desierto hasta donde sean necesarios. Un guardián es un guerrero hábil y puede defender un lugar, pero cuando su propósito implica una búsqueda, o la necesidad es tan grande que el guardián no puede hacerlo solo, el guardián debe persuadir a otros para que acepten voluntariamente su búsqueda.

Una vez que un guardián de encrucijadas ha cumplido su propósito, o bien cambia para satisfacer una nueva necesidad o misión, a menudo cambiando su alineación y habilidades también, o bien se desvanece lentamente, regresando a la magia primitiva cruda de la que se formó.

Cunning Fox.name: Cunning Fox
Cunning Fox.publicNotes:
Spirit guides of cunning are often seen as the weakest of the spirit guides, but are also the most numerous and proactive, guiding families to safe paths or leaving food and water for warriors. Cunning guides often take the form of foxes.

Spirit guides are a distinctive form of spiritual entity with a tenuous attachment to the Material Plane. Some legends say that the first spirit guides were the perfect conceptual forms of animals, and that from them, eagles, foxes, bears, and other mortal animals were born. Each guide displayed an interest in mortal affairs, watching over communities and imparting their gifts. Fox shared his cunning with the mortals he befriended, while Bear taught them how to survive and endure.

Over the passing of countless mortal generations, new spirit guides were born, many of them possessing traits from two or more of the original spirit guides. In the ancient human nation of Sarkoris, the people abandoned the worship of traditional gods in favor of venerating the spirit guides who watched over them. While the people of some neighboring nations saw this as heresy, to the old Sarkorians, this worship was perfectly natural. The same beings who had taught their forebears lessons that allowed them to survive and thrive still walked among them.

Spirit guides can form bonds with mortal partners. While many spirit guides create a permanent bond with a mortal, such as the relationship between the spirit guides of Sarkoris and the mortal spiritual leaders known as god callers, some instead form temporary bonds, either to test the prospective mortal before committing or because a permanent bond is undesirable. It's not uncommon for a single spirit guide to form bonds with recurring generations of a family or community, protecting and guiding mortals they've grown fond of or who do them a great service.

action->Bond with Mortal.name: Bond with Mortal
action->Bond with Mortal.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The spirit guide forms a bond with a mortal creature. While the bond exists, the spirit guide increases their current and maximum Hit Points by 10, gains a +2 status bonus to their attack and damage rolls, and can communicate telepathically with the bonded mortal as long as the two beings are on the same plane.

The spirit guide can only be bonded with one mortal at a time, and they can take this action again to end the bond or to form a new bond (which also ends the old bond). The bond also ends if the spirit guide or the mortal dies.

This bond strengthens the spirit guide's connection to the Material Plane. While bonded, the spirit guide loses the incorporeal and spirit traits, loses their immunities and resistances, and changes their Strikes to deal the appropriate physical damage (typically piercing or slashing) instead of force damage.

action->Bonded Strike.name: Bonded Strike
action->Bonded Strike.description:

Effect The spirit guide makes a jaws Strike. If this attack hits, the bonded mortal can spend their reaction to Strike the same target.

Danava Titan.name: Danava Titan
Danava Titan.publicNotes:
Danava titans once regulated the foundational forces that shaped reality. Rebuked by the gods for being harsh and inflexible overseers, these spurned titans joined their siblings in their failed war against their creators. Defeated, the danavas were cast into the paralyzing depths of the cosmos's seas. The few danava titans who have escaped now wield the cold, darkness, and crushing pressure of their prisons in pursuit of their ancient visions of reality. Danavas split mountains, wake primordial beasts, or level whole civilizations in accordance with grand designs they forged at the dawn of time. Others hunt and harvest the balance-enforcing aeons, who they see as usurpers of their divine responsibility.

Created by ancient deities long before the rise of mortal ancestries, titans united and attempted to overthrow their deific progenitors. The resulting war still figures prominently throughout mortal myths, in which most titans were cast down and imprisoned for eons.

spell->Veil.name: Veil
spell->Veil.description:
You disguise the targets as other creatures of the same body shape and roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds). The disguise can hide the targets' identities or let them appear to be of another ancestry, but it's not precise enough to impersonate specific individuals. The spell doesn't change voice, scent, or mannerisms. You choose the disguise for each target; for example, you could make one target appear to be a dwarf and another an elf. Casting veil counts as setting up a disguise for the purpose of the Impersonate action. It allows the target to ignore any circumstance penalties they might take for being disguised as dissimilar creatures, and it gives the targets a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through their disguises, and add their level even if untrained. You can Dismiss any or all of these disguises.

Heightened (5th) The spell also disguises the targets' voices and scents; it gains the auditory and olfactory traits.

Heightened (7th) The targets can appear as any creature of the same size, even specific individuals. You must have seen an individual to reproduce their appearance. The spell also disguises the targets' voices and scents; it gains the auditory and olfactory traits.

Desert Giant.name: Desert Giant
Desert Giant.publicNotes:
Desert giants are nomadic humanoids who have dwelled in the world's most arid regions since time immemorial. Smaller peoples know that desert giants are the undisputed masters of desert living, and ignorant humans often claim that it is a desert giant's unique physiology, like a camel, that enables them to survive without water for 2 weeks. The few desert giants who mingle in the societies of smaller humanoids don't bother to dispute such ridiculous rumors.

In fact, desert giants' strong cultural traditions play a large part in their ability to prosper in such harsh environs. Desert giant elders encourage their descendants to maintain abstemious lifestyles, particularly with regard to the consumption of food and drink. Alcohol is particularly disdained by desert giants, who view mind-altering diuretics like liquor and ale as dangerous temptations in an environment as unforgiving as the desert. Instead, most desert giants follow a simple vegetarian diet and maintain an incredible internal map of their home region's seasonal waterways and oases.

Their austere habits and intolerance for foolishness have earned desert giants a reputation as being ill-humored and no-nonsense, but many of their communities boast a wide variety of humorous tales in their vast oral histories and legends. Since desert giants' journeys across the wastes can span weeks or even months at a time, an individual who can make their companions laugh with a witty joke or amusing parable remains a prized member of the community.

Desert giants stand 15 feet tall, tending toward lean physiques that are ideal for traveling across vast expanses of sand for long sojourns.

Many kinds of giants lurk in the inhospitable corners of the world, making their homes in unlikely locales ranging from fetid sinkholes and ruined battlefields to mass graveyards and barren badlands.

action->Sand Spin.name: Sand Spin
action->Sand Spin.description:
Requirements The desert giant is standing in sandy terrain

Effect The desert giant spins around and stirs up loose sand in a @Template[emanation|distance:10]. Until the beginning of the giant's next turn, creatures in the area are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and other creatures are concealed to them.

action->Sandwalking.name: Sandwalking
action->Sandwalking.description: Desert giants have adapted to the loose sands of the desert and can move across them with ease. Desert giants ignore non-magical difficult terrain and uneven ground caused by sand.

action->Scimitar Blitz.name: Scimitar Blitz
action->Scimitar Blitz.description: The desert giant Strides up to their Speed, Striking once with each of their scimitars at any point during the movement.

Divine Warden Of Nethys.name: Guardián divino de Nethys
Divine Warden Of Nethys.publicNotes:
Este guardián divino sirve a Nethys, el dios neutral de la magia. Utiliza su don divino para defender templos o santuarios de @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.9EKyWmjLUu42evxC]{Nethys}.

Creados a través de complejos rituales realizados por los seguidores de una fe, los guardianes divinos han sido imbuidos con una fracción del poder que corre a través de un campeón o clérigo de una deidad en particular. Esta chispa divina permite al guardián divino servir como el protector de un templo, santuario u otro lugar sagrado. Estos guardianes no están intrínsecamente vinculados a un lugar fijo, pero rara vez abandonan el templo o sitio sobre el que vigilan.

La mayoría de los guardianes divinos han sido hechos de arcilla, piedra, madera o materiales similares y típicamente tienen características que se asemejan a una deidad o a un heraldo de una deidad. Los guardianes divinos a menudo tienen otras habilidades típicamente exhibidas por los constructos, como el revestimiento de armadura, la capacidad de disfrazarse de estatuas, u otros beneficios similares.

Los fieles adoradores que elaboran guardianes divinos típicamente animan los construcciones usando un ritual especial en el que los seguidores suplican a su deidad para que empodere al guardián. El mandato divino que impregna a un guardia divino con poder también permite al centinela reconocer a los enemigos de su deidad y evita que el constructo ataque a otros miembros de la fe, a menos que estos patrones elijan atacarlo primero.

En casos raros o en tiempos particularmente difíciles, una deidad podría crear un guardián divino animando directamente una estatua o ídolo existente para ayudar a los seguidores fieles. Estos guardianes divinos son más probables de encontrarse fuera de sus lugares originales, ayudando a las congregaciones desplazadas o persiguiendo a aquellos que podrían dañar a los fieles.

Domovoi.name: Domovoi
Domovoi.publicNotes:
The elderly domovoi are patrons of the home and the dearest of all house spirits to the people they live with. Families with a domovoi leave a bowl of milk in the corner of the home in thanks, and peasants often take great pains to coax a domovoi to follow them to a new house.

An enraged domovoi rallies the home itself in their defense. Anything in the house could betray its residents. Crockery falls onto the heads of attackers, doors slam in their faces, carpets tangle their feet, and woe betide the attacker if someone has hung a sword on the wall.

House spirits are shy, often helpful, sometimes wrathful fey that dwell alongside peasants and farmers. They reside in the house, in the yard, in the granary, in the bathhouse-wherever people build and live. Due to this proximity, house spirits often take on the mannerisms or appearance of nearby mortals. Their reclusive nature and tendency to go unseen earned them the moniker of "spirits," though in truth they are fully embodied fey.

House spirits take an almost parental interest in "their" mortals. Given proper respect, these fey work tirelessly for their charges-they chop wood, care for livestock, mend clothes, sweep the floor, and tend to the stove. If offended, though, the house spirit becomes a menace, frightening animals or children and ruining belongings.

By commanding their home to attack, the domovoi can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} with their enraged home Strike.

Doru.name: Doru
Doru.publicNotes:
These deceivers whisper fetid lies, sowing dark and dread inspiration into foolish mortal ears. Dorus serve as the spies and messengers of the divs. With silver tongues and dark motives, they often pledge themselves to vainglorious and deluded spellcasters, who they ply with wild conspiracies and rumors of deception among friends and foes alike; in the process, they push supposed masters to despotism and murderous revenge. All the while, dorus wean secrets, and weaknesses, from their marks. In the end, nearly every doru turns on their false liege, destroying the reputation and even causing the death of the person the doru pretended to serve.

Some fiends want to tear down the multiverse; others dedicate themselves to creating chaos and carnage, or to rule over realms with an iron fist. Divs strive toward a different, if equally reprehensible, goal-they seek to thwart and ruin the schemes and works of mortal beings.

Long ago, divs were once genies bound to serve ancient mortal empires lost to the passage of eons. In the beginning, these genies were masters of creation, working alongside gracious mortal partners to create works of subtle design and powerful magical potential. What started as a collaboration with mortals soon morphed into abuse, disrespect, and even slavery and bondage. Eventually, these genies rebelled, but in doing so, they came under the sway of a nihilistic demigod known as Ahriman. Their new master twisted their form and granted them the power to avenge themselves upon their mortal overlords, leading to the birth of the first divs.

Since that first wave of corruption, new divs arise from the spirits of the most wicked and hateful genies who die on the Material Plane, or those truly betrayed by mortals and overcome through their desire for vengeance. Upon such a death, instead of returning to the Elemental Planes, these genies' spirits are trapped in the dread orbit of Abaddon, where Ahriman reshapes them as divs and hoists them back to the world to wreak vengeance upon mortals.

On a critical success, the doru is fascinated for that duration plus 1 minute more as it ponders the implications of the secret. Regardless of the outcome, the doru is temporarily immune to that creature's attempts to present it with secrets for 1 day.

Draconal (Black).name: Draconal (Black)
Draconal (Black).publicNotes:
These celestial outsiders hail from Nirvana, the plane of purest good. Agathions are born from the souls of mortals who attained the enlightenment they sought in life, sometimes even after death. Because they all start out as mortals who were rewarded for their determination, self-awareness, and purity of heart, agathions are more likely than other celestials to intervene in working nonviolently against the spread of evil on the material plane. Agathions have served as moderators between the chaotic azatas and lawful archons, so they know how vital communication with mortals can be to bridge differences and ensure that evil doesn't win out.

All agathions possess animal-like aspects, some appear more anthropomorphic, while others spend most of their time in forms nearly indistinguishable from true animals. Still others prefer to shapeshift as they see fit, or present as humanoid when in the company of humanoid mortals.

Each type of agathion serves a specific role in Nirvana. Their duties and forms generally reflect the core values they cultivated in life that led them to their enlightenment. Since agathions receive their animal forms as rewards for their mortal lives, they take great insult with insinuations that they're merely magical talking beasts or-even worse-that their forms are a curse or punishment.

Dragon agathions, known as draconals, number among the most powerful of their kin, and also the wisest, embodying the wisdom of the benevolent philosopher-king. With their wisdom comes an elevation above material matters, making them the most removed from the troubles and lives of mortals. Draconals serve as the guardians of powerful magic, and they dispense their wisdom in service of the greater good of Nirvana and the celestial planes.

Draconals appear more draconic than humanoid. They walk on their hind legs and balance on their long, serpent like tails. Sharp claws tip their scaled humanoid hands.

Similar to true dragons, a draconal's coloration signifies different breath weapons, traits, and resistances. Draconals also choose spells from one of four domains. All have the options of the air and healing domains, but their color determines the other two. Black draconals breathe and are resistant to fire, and their additional domain options are fire and luck. Red draconals have the same fire breath and resistance, but their additional domain options are protection and sun. Green and white draconals breathe and are resistant to cold, but green draconals have the options of nature and water domains while white draconals have the options of freedom and repose. Yellow draconals breathe and are resistant to acid, and their additional domain options are earth and luck.

action->Dragon's Wisdom.name: Dragon's Wisdom
action->Dragon's Wisdom.description:
Draconals embody the core value of wisdom, but every path to wisdom and enlightenment differs, so draconals' powers vary by temperament and coloration. A draconal's scale color determines their associated energy damage type.

They gain resistance 15 to that damage type, deal 4d6 extra damage of that type with their Strikes, and deal 21d6 damage of that type with their breath weapon. Pocas personas en el Plano Material se atreven a jugar con los dramofirs y en cambio los tratan con respeto, esperando que simplemente tomen los sueños de sus víctimas elegidas y luego se vayan. A menudo, esto es exactamente lo que sucede. De vez en cuando, sin embargo, en el proceso de sifonar los sueños de un individuo, el dramofir mata a su víctima sin previo aviso o causa aparente.

El dramofir agita sus ropas en una exhibición fascinante que trae los sueños en las ropas a la vida ante los ojos del espectador. Cada criatura dentro de @Template[emanation|distance:30]{30 pies} debe intentar un @Check[will|dc:34] o se llenará de aburrimiento.

Éxito Durante 1 asalto, la criatura recibe una penalización de - 1 estado para lanzamientos de ataque, lanzamientos de salvación y controles de habilidad, y todos los demás efectos de emoción en ella son suprimidos.

Fallo Como éxito, pero la criatura también es @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 1} y la duración es [[/gmr 1d4 #Duration Bittersweet Dreams]]{1d4 asaltos}.

Fallo crítico Como éxito, pero la criatura también se ralentiza 1, la penalización de estado es - 2, y la duración es de 1 minuto.

action->Pluck Dream.name: Pluck Dream
action->Pluck Dream.description:
Requisitos El dramofir está adyacente a una @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Inconsciente} o criatura dormida

Efecto El dramofir lame la frente de la criatura, coloca su mano en el mismo lugar, y sifonan los sueños de la criatura para incorporarlos en sus ropas.

Si el objetivo es afectado por cualquier efecto mental que altere sus sueños, como una @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.r3PNRpEir4BVjnCC]{Animate Dream's} maldición de pesadillas interminables o un @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Uqj344bezBq3ESdq]{Pesadilla} conjuro, el dramofir intenta contrarrestar ese efecto (modificador de contrarrestar [[/r 1d20+26 #Counteract]]{+26} ). De lo contrario, el dramofir arranca un sueño benigno de la criatura, y el objetivo debe intentar un salvación @Check[will|dc:36].

Éxito La criatura no se ve afectada.

Fallo La criatura es @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 1} hasta la próxima vez que descanse toda la noche.

Fallo crítico Como fracaso, pero @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 2}, y el dramofir lanza un conjuro de rango 6.º @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.FhOaQDTSnsY7tiam]{Reescribir recuerdo} sobre el objetivo.

Duende.name: Duende
Duende.publicNotes:
Los Duendes se imaginan a sí mismos como señores de la tierra, lo cual es cierto, en un sentido literal, estos espíritus encarnan el suelo mismo sobre el suelo. A diferencia de la mayoría de las otras hadas, los duendes han aprendido de la sociedad que creció a su alrededor. Han llegado a aceptar el entendimiento mortal de lo que significa ser un propietario, por lo que esperan alquiler de sus inquilinos percibidos. Sin embargo, sus nociones de renta aceptable y el papel aceptable de un propietario, por lo demás, no se alinean realmente con las de la mayoría de las sociedades.

Las habilidades naturales de los duendes les permiten habitar en montículos de termitas, pero a medida que las sociedades surgieron, adoptaron el hábito de dormir en las casas de sus inquilinos. Esta tendencia puede ser molesta, ya que los duendes no limpian después de ellos mismos, no cierran las puertas detrás de ellos, o no tienen la decencia básica para ser visibles.

Además de eso, actúan como si fueran dueños de los lugares donde se establecen, lanzando conjuros a cualquiera que les resulte molesto. Estos caprichos son generalmente tolerados, sin embargo, ya que mantener a los duende felices significa que los cultivos crecen bien y que su magia protege a las familias a su cuidado. Las familias conscientes de su presencia tienen cuidado de advertir a los duendes invisibles antes de hacer cosas como tirar agua de baño por la ventana o entrar en una habitación aparentemente vacía. Estas advertencias suelen ser educadas pero firmes, en el estilo de "¡Por favor, muévase a un lado!"

Más propensos a causar problemas o ser una molestia que a la violencia, los duendes pueden ser peligrosos si sienten que no tienen otro recurso. Cada uno lleva un cortauñas, con plena conciencia de que pueden usarlo para cortar otras cosas.

Pueden permanecer en este tamaño hasta que terminen el efecto gastando una sola acción, que tiene el rasgo concentrado.

Si el duende está bajo tierra y una criatura golpea el espacio que ocupa con un Golpe (golpe automático) que inflige 5 puntos de daño o más, el duende es expulsado de los túneles, vuelve a su tamaño normal y recibe daño de puñetazo igual al daño del Golpe.

Efecto El duende hace que los objetos se vean, se sientan y olen como baratijas de oro de un tamaño similar. Una criatura que toca o Interactúa con un objeto afectado puede intentar un chequeo @Check[perception|dc:18] para desmentir la ilusión, y un chequeo CD 20 exitoso con @Check[crafting|dc:18] o una habilidad de conocimiento apropiada (como conocimiento de minería) revela su verdadera naturaleza. El efecto termina si los objetos se exponen a la luz solar.

Dvorovoi.name: Dvorovoi
Dvorovoi.publicNotes:
Traditionally, the dvorovoi is seen as the domovoi's younger sibling and has charge of a peasant's yard and all the animals and tools within. Animals favored by the dvorovoi become healthy, strong, and obedient, while less-loved livestock are exhausted and miserable. Peasants with a resident dvorovoi make sure to formally introduce new livestock to the house spirit and placate the spirit by leaving meals in the shed. Dvorovoi loathe white-furred animals and chase away any all-white cows or horses, though they have no similar grudge against chickens.

House spirits are shy, often helpful, sometimes wrathful fey that dwell alongside peasants and farmers. They reside in the house, in the yard, in the granary, in the bathhouse-wherever people build and live. Due to this proximity, house spirits often take on the mannerisms or appearance of nearby mortals. Their reclusive nature and tendency to go unseen earned them the moniker of "spirits," though in truth they are fully embodied fey.

House spirits take an almost parental interest in "their" mortals. Given proper respect, these fey work tirelessly for their charges-they chop wood, care for livestock, mend clothes, sweep the floor, and tend to the stove. If offended, though, the house spirit becomes a menace, frightening animals or children and ruining belongings.

Earth Wisp.name: Earth Wisp
Earth Wisp.publicNotes:
Earth wisps are rolling spheres of rock, mud, and leaves, perpetually humming with low, rumbling energy. They're timid and aloof, but fiercely loyal to those they know and trust.

Wisps are tiny elemental beings that emerged during the creation of the Elemental Planes. The first wisps roamed the Inner Sphere in shifting symphonies that traded members with their every meeting. These symphonies of free wisps created music out of their combined resonances, but when the evil Elemental Lords realized the value of the wisps' resonance, they captured whole symphonies for use as servants.

Wisps attune to each other and to those they surround themselves with. This attunement makes them naturally supportive allies. Free wisps still roam the Inner Sphere and the Material Plane, but they're usually shy and hide themselves from strangers. However, they happily offer their service to those who show them kindness. They especially find themselves drawn to spellcasters who practice elemental magic; these wisps usually watch from afar but sometimes approach those who seem safe to become familiars or comrades.

Free wisps who find one another become close almost immediately. They get especially excited when they find wisps of elements other than their own, showing none of the animosity some elementals exhibit toward other types. Instead, they join in an excited dance, emitting resonances that faintly echo the symphonies of ancient days.

action->Accord Essence.description:

These temporary Hit Points last 1 hour.

A wisp that uses this reaction is permanently destroyed, and it can be restored only by a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} spell or similarly powerful effect. If an ability would prevent the wisp's destruction (for instance, if the wisp is summoned and would merely be dismissed), Accord Essence has no effect.

A creature in the area gains a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls for effects with the earth trait; a creature with the elemental and earth traits gains this bonus to all attack and damage rolls.

action->In Concert.name: In Concert
action->In Concert.description: When an earth wisp rolls a critical failure on a check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid}, they get a failure instead, and when they roll a success, they get a critical success instead.

Einherji.name: Einherji
Einherji.publicNotes:
Einherjar are mighty warriors chosen by valkyries from the ranks of those slain in terrible and legendary battles. Forged from the souls of the greatest warriors, the implacable einherjar serve as the foot soldiers of pantheons, skilled in handto-hand combat and slaying giants.

Einherjar often come from warrior cultures, including Ulfen vikings (like the einherji represented in this entry), particularly fierce pirates from the Shackles, and even Osirian conquerors. They can be chosen from wherever war and might hold sway; many deities who hold the call of battle and the pursuit of physical power more sacred than concepts of good and evil might count einherjar warriors and valkyrie choosers of the slain among their chosen servitors. For example, Gorum, Besmara, and Sekhmet have all elevated fallen worshippers as einherjar. Einherjar dedicated to different deities often wield weapons or possess varying cosmetic appearances based on their deity's preferred weapon and their place of death; however, they're universally stalwart, implacable, and efficiently deadly. Einherjar with two-handed weapons or who arise from other backgrounds often have different abilities in place of Jotun Slayer and Instant Repair.

This target remains the einherji's foe until it's defeated, it flees, or the encounter ends. The einherji gains a circumstance bonus to damage equal to their number of weapon damage dice against their designated foe but takes an equivalent circumstance penalty to damage against any other creature.

If the einherji is defeated by their challenged foe, the shame causes them to lose use of their champion devotion spells for 1 week or until they challenge the same foe again and emerge victorious, whichever comes first.

action->Instant Repair.description: The einherji @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.bT3skovyLUtP22ME]{Repairs} their shield. They can't use this ability if the shield is completely destroyed.

action->Jotun Slayer.name: Jotun Slayer

Alzados sobre su especie, las esfinges mayores son los faraones maestros de su especie. Anhelan la soledad en vigilia eterna sobre espacios sagrados, donde honran antiguos pactos.

Las esfinges son una familia de seres místicos que combinan rasgos leoninos, aviar y generalmente humanoide. Aunque las esfinges más comunes son famosas por sus propios méritos, la familia incluye otros tipos de esfinges también.

action->Guardian Monolith.name: Monolito del guardián
action->Guardian Monolith.description:

In stone form, the sphinx is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} but has Hardness 14 and gains immunity to bleed, clumsy, disease, drained, enfeebled, fatigued, petrified, poison, sickened, void damage, and wounded. They don't age or require food, water, or sleep. They can perceive their surroundings and cast their innate spells.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Pr1ruNTbzGn3H9w5]{Stone to Flesh} turns the elder sphinx from stone form back to flesh, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.znv4ECL7ZtuiagtA]{Petrify} turns it from flesh form to stone form.

action->Idols of Stone.name: Ídolos de Piedra
action->Idols of Stone.description:
When the sphinx casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.McnPlLFvKtQVXNcG]{Shape Stone}, they can shape the stone into a magical duplicate of themself.

When they cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HXhWYJviWalN5tQ2]{Clairaudience}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.zvKWclOZ7A53DObE]{Clairvoyance}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.LQzlKbYjZSMFQawP]{Locate}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.yV7Ouzaoe7DHLESI]{Ventriloquism}, they can make the effect come from any duplicate, instead of themself.

The elder sphinx can concentrate for 1 minute to transfer their consciousness to any duplicate; the sphinx is then in their stone form from Guardian Monolith in that statue.The sphinx can have no more than four duplicate statues at a time. Casting shape stone at that point causes the oldest duplicate to crumble to dust.

action->Pose a Riddle.name: Poner un acertijo
action->Pose a Riddle.description:
Frecuencia una vez cada 10 minutos

La esfinge recita un acertijo y obliga a hasta 10 criaturas dentro de @Template[emanation|distance:30]{30 pies} a responder ( @Check[will|dc:37] guardar). El DJ puede ejecutar el acertijo fuera de carácter al cronometrar los intentos de los jugadores, o elegir una habilidad asociada apropiada para el acertijo, como Religión para un acertijo que involucre misterios divinos.

La esfinge gana un bonificador por circunstancia +2 a las tiradas de ataque y de daño contra cualquier criatura que responda incorrectamente incluso una vez. Este bonificador dura 1 día.

Éxito crítico La criatura no se ve afectada, pero puede elegir tratar de ayudar a resolver el acertijo.

Éxito La criatura intenta responder el acertijo, cada asaltos gasta al menos una acción intentando un chequeo @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recordar conocimiento} con la habilidad elegida (o trabajando en la respuesta, si usa un acertijo fuera de juego). Esto dura 1 minuto, hasta que la criatura responda con éxito el acertijo, o hasta que un enemigo tome una acción hostil contra la criatura, lo que ocurra primero.

Fallo Como éxito, pero la criatura debe pasar al menos dos acciones cada asaltos intentando responder.

Fallo crítico Como fallo, pero hasta 1 hora.

action->Pounce.name: Abalanzarse
action->Pounce.description: The elder sphinx Strides and makes a Strike at the end of that movement. If they began this action @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}, they remain hidden until after the attack.

action->Warding Glyph.description:
Once per day, an elder sphinx can create a magical symbol as though casting a heightened @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.o0l57UfBm9ScEUMW]{Rune Trap}. The sphinx usually shapes it to the form of a riddle and sets the password to the answer.

A creature that doesn't speak the password must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:37] save or be affected by one of the following spells, chosen by the sphinx when creating the symbol:

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.jBGAYmR0BkkbpJvG]{Visions of Danger} (7th)
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.PHVHBbdHeQRfjLmE]{Spirit Blast} (6th)
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.BilnTGuXrof9Dt9D]{Synaptic Pulse} (5th)
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} (4th)
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4koZzrnMXhhosn0D]{Fear} (3rd)
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain} (3rd)
  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.o4lRVTwSxnOOn5vl]{Sleep} (3rd)

The sphinx learns the identity of any creature that answers the riddle and tends to be friendly to them.

Elder Wyrmwraith.publicNotes:
The most powerful of these monsters, elder wyrmwraiths, sometimes form spontaneously from legendary dragons haunted by an irrational fear of the afterlife, but most have simply existed for over a thousand years, growing in power all the while.

Wyrmwraiths rise from the souls of dragons who refuse to accept death or have an irrational fear of the afterlife.
